```{r}

#| include: false

# Lightweight, render-time setup. This is the ONLY chunk that runs on a normal
# render: it loads a few small packages so the on-disk tables/figure can be
# displayed, and sets the master switch below.
#

# once (or run the appendix chunks interactively), render, then set it back.
run_analysis <- FALSE
embed_violins <- TRUE   # TRUE = single self-contained HTML; FALSE = sidecar *-violin/ folder

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(readr)
  library(knitr)

  library(htmltools)

# --- Violin explorer helpers (render-time; scans on-disk PNGs) ----------------
extract_document_genes <- function(qmd_path) {
  lines <- readLines(qmd_path, warn = FALSE)
  cut <- which(grepl("^# Code & Provenance", lines))
  if (length(cut)) lines <- lines[seq_len(cut[1] - 1)]
  txt <- paste(lines, collapse = "\n")

  genes <- character()
  for (pat in c(
    "\\*\\*([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]+)\\*\\*",
    "\\*([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]+)\\*",
    "\\| \\*([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]+)\\* \\|"
  )) {
    m <- regmatches(txt, gregexpr(pat, txt, perl = TRUE))[[1]]
    if (length(m)) genes <- c(genes, gsub("\\*+|\\|", "", m))
  }
  if (grepl("ENSMUSG00000095041", txt)) genes <- c(genes, "ENSMUSG00000095041")

  pairs <- regmatches(txt, gregexpr("([A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]+)/([A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]+)", txt, perl = TRUE))[[1]]
  if (length(pairs)) {
    split_pairs <- strsplit(pairs, "/", fixed = TRUE)
    genes <- c(genes, unlist(split_pairs))
  }

  exclude <- c(
    "AMY", "HYP", "BLA", "CeA", "MEA", "LA", "BST", "COA", "ENT", "SUM", "MPN",
    "AVPV", "POA", "ZI", "AHN", "LHA", "VMH", "ARH", "PVH", "CRH", "TRH", "GnRH",
    "SCFA", "SCFAs", "ASD", "GWAS", "LTP", "LTD", "CICR", "ERK", "Akt", "PTEN",
    "PP2A", "PLZF", "Dec1", "SK2", "Kv", "HDAC", "NCoR", "CaMKII", "ISH", "IHC",
    "FISH", "SeqFISH", "CellChat", "gProfiler", "scFEA", "Augur", "EdgeR", "DESeq2",
    "MAST", "mTORC1", "AMPK", "WildR", "SPF", "GABA", "Robo", "cork", "GTP", "Ras",
    "MAPK", "PI3K", "RNA", "ncRNA", "ATAC", "Cre", "Zeitgeber", "IP3", "MM", "SDMN",
    "KO", "TrkB", "Calcium", "Ca2", "region", "level", "dissociation", "Mechanistic",
    "Functional", "Behavioral", "Reading", "Source", "Key", "Figure", "How",
    "gene", "tissue", "systemic", "Kv2"
  )

  genes <- unique(trimws(genes))
  genes <- genes[nzchar(genes) & !genes %in% exclude]
  sort(genes)
}

scan_violin_catalog <- function(violin_root, fig_base = "../figures/DEG/snRNASeq/top_hits/supertype") {
  if (!dir.exists(violin_root)) return(tibble())

  files <- list.files(violin_root, pattern = "\\.png$", recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)
  if (!length(files)) return(tibble())

  parsed <- lapply(files, function(f) {
    parts <- strsplit(normalizePath(f), .Platform$file.sep, fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
    idx <- which(parts == "supertype")
    if (!length(idx) || length(parts) < idx + 3) return(NULL)

    tissue <- parts[idx + 1]
    celltype_clean <- parts[idx + 2]
    fname <- parts[idx + 3]
    m <- regexec("^(.+)_(WildR-UP|SPF-UP)_([A-Z]+)_(.+)\\.png$", fname)
    reg <- regmatches(fname, m)[[1]]
    if (length(reg) < 5) return(NULL)

    tibble(
      gene = reg[2],
      direction = reg[3],
      tissue = reg[4],
      celltype_clean = reg[5],
      celltype_label = gsub("_", " ", reg[5]),
      rel_path = file.path(fig_base, tissue, celltype_clean, fname)
    )
  })

  parsed <- purrr::compact(parsed)
  bind_rows(parsed)
}

png_data_uri <- function(path) {
  paste0(
    "data:image/png;base64,",
    jsonlite::base64_enc(readBin(path, "raw", n = file.info(path)$size))
  )
}

knitr_input_dir <- function() {
  input <- knitr::current_input()
  if (!is.null(input) && nzchar(input)) {
    return(dirname(normalizePath(input, mustWork = FALSE)))
  }
  root <- knitr::opts_knit$get("root.dir")
  if (!is.null(root) && nzchar(root)) return(normalizePath(root, mustWork = FALSE))
  getwd()
}

violin_asset_paths <- function(qmd_path = NULL) {
  input <- knitr::current_input()
  if (!is.null(input) && nzchar(input)) {
    stem <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(input))
    input_dir <- knitr_input_dir()
  } else if (!is.null(qmd_path) && nzchar(qmd_path)) {
    stem <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(qmd_path))
    input_dir <- knitr_input_dir()
    if (!file.exists(file.path(input_dir, qmd_path))) {
      candidate <- normalizePath(qmd_path, mustWork = FALSE)
      if (file.exists(candidate)) {
        stem <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(candidate))
        input_dir <- dirname(candidate)
      }
    }
  } else {
    stem <- "0X_DEG_Analysis-top-hits"
    input_dir <- knitr_input_dir()
  }
  # Outside *_files so embed-resources does not delete violin assets after render.
  asset_abs <- file.path(input_dir, paste0(stem, "-violin"))
  asset_rel <- paste0(stem, "-violin")
  list(abs = asset_abs, rel = asset_rel, input_dir = input_dir)
}

ensure_violin_symlink <- function(violin_root, qmd_path = NULL) {
  paths <- violin_asset_paths(qmd_path = qmd_path)
  dir.create(dirname(paths$abs), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  target <- normalizePath(violin_root, mustWork = FALSE)

  if (dir.exists(paths$abs)) {
    link_target <- tryCatch(Sys.readlink(paths$abs), error = function(e) "")
    if (link_target == target) return(paths)
    unlink(paths$abs, recursive = TRUE)
  }

  ok <- file.symlink(target, paths$abs)
  if (!ok) {
    warning("Could not symlink violin assets; falling back to relative figures path.")
    paths$rel <- file.path("..", "figures", "DEG", "snRNASeq", "top_hits", "supertype")
    paths$abs <- normalizePath(
      file.path(paths$input_dir, paths$rel),
      mustWork = FALSE
    )
  }
  paths
}

render_violin_explorer <- function(
  catalog, doc_genes, violin_root,
  qmd_path = NULL, embed_violins = TRUE,
  qmd_label = "display-violin-explorer"
) {
  if (!nrow(catalog)) {
    return('<p class="violin-explorer-empty">Violin plot directory not found. Run appendix chunk <code>cell-violin-plots</code> to generate PNGs.</p>')
  }

  fig_base <- if (embed_violins) "" else ensure_violin_symlink(violin_root, qmd_path = qmd_path)$rel
  catalog <- scan_violin_catalog(violin_root, fig_base = fig_base)

  hits <- catalog %>%
    filter(gene %in% doc_genes) %>%
    arrange(gene, tissue, celltype_label, direction)

  hits <- hits %>%
    mutate(
      fname = paste0(gene, "_", direction, "_", tissue, "_", celltype_clean, ".png"),
      src_abs = file.path(violin_root, tissue, celltype_clean, fname)
    ) %>%
    filter(file.exists(src_abs))

  if (!nrow(hits)) {
    return('<p class="violin-explorer-empty">No violin plots match genes named in this report.</p>')
  }

  hits <- hits %>%
    mutate(path = if (embed_violins) vapply(src_abs, png_data_uri, character(1)) else rel_path)

  genes_avail <- hits %>%
    count(gene, name = "n_hits") %>%
    arrange(gene)

  payload <- list(
    genes = genes_avail$gene,
    counts = setNames(as.list(genes_avail$n_hits), genes_avail$gene),
    entries = hits %>%
      transmute(
        gene, direction, tissue,
        celltype = celltype_label,
        key = paste(gene, tissue, celltype_clean, direction, sep = "|"),
        path = .data$path
      ) %>%
      split(.$gene, drop = TRUE) %>%
      lapply(function(df) df[, c("key", "tissue", "celltype", "direction", "path")])
  )

  json_txt <- jsonlite::toJSON(payload, auto_unbox = TRUE, null = "null")

  paste0(
    '

<script>
(function () {
  const catalog = JSON.parse(document.getElementById("ve-catalog").textContent);
  const geneSel = document.getElementById("ve-gene");
  const tissueSel = document.getElementById("ve-tissue");
  const cellSel = document.getElementById("ve-celltype");
  const plotImg = document.getElementById("ve-plot");
  const hitCount = document.getElementById("ve-hit-count");
  const dirBadge = document.getElementById("ve-direction");

  function populateGenes() {
    geneSel.innerHTML = "";
    catalog.genes.forEach((g) => {
      const opt = document.createElement("option");
      opt.value = g;
      opt.textContent = `${g} (${catalog.counts[g]} supertypes)`;
      geneSel.appendChild(opt);
    });
  }

  function filteredEntries() {
    const gene = geneSel.value;
    const tissue = tissueSel.value;
    let rows = catalog.entries[gene] || [];
    if (tissue !== "all") rows = rows.filter((r) => r.tissue === tissue);
    return rows;
  }

  function populateCelltypes() {
    const rows = filteredEntries();
    cellSel.innerHTML = "";
    rows.forEach((r) => {
      const opt = document.createElement("option");
      opt.value = r.key;
      opt.textContent = `[${r.tissue}] ${r.celltype}`;
      cellSel.appendChild(opt);
    });
    hitCount.textContent = `${rows.length} significant supertype${rows.length === 1 ? "" : "s"}`;
    if (rows.length) {
      plotImg.src = rows[0].path;
      dirBadge.textContent = rows[0].direction;
      dirBadge.className = "violin-badge " + (rows[0].direction === "WildR-UP" ? "wildr" : "spf");
    } else {
      plotImg.removeAttribute("src");
      dirBadge.textContent = "No hits in filter";
      dirBadge.className = "violin-badge";
    }
  }

  function syncPlot() {
    const gene = geneSel.value;
    const tissue = tissueSel.value;
    let rows = catalog.entries[gene] || [];
    if (tissue !== "all") rows = rows.filter((r) => r.tissue === tissue);
    const row = rows.find((r) => r.key === cellSel.value);
    if (row) {
      plotImg.src = row.path;
      dirBadge.textContent = row.direction;
      dirBadge.className = "violin-badge " + (row.direction === "WildR-UP" ? "wildr" : "spf");
    }
  }

  populateGenes();
  populateCelltypes();
  geneSel.addEventListener("change", () => { populateCelltypes(); });
  tissueSel.addEventListener("change", () => { populateCelltypes(); });
  cellSel.addEventListener("change", syncPlot);
})();
</script>
'
  )
```

## Overview

This report presents cell-type-resolved differential expression between WildR (naturalistic microbiome) and SPF (specific pathogen-free) mice across Allen Brain Atlas supertypes in amygdala (AMY) and hypothalamus (HYP). The top 75 DEGs, visualized in the clustered dot-plot heatmap below, reveal a striking **region-level dissociation**: hypothalamic hits are often pan-regional (dense rows spanning many supertypes), while amygdalar hits are supertype-restricted. Five convergent biological storylines emerge from the heatmap — pan-hypothalamic translational hyperactivation in SPF (Cmss1/Lars2), amygdalar synaptic remodeling, calcium excitability shifts, epigenetic reprogramming, and hypothalamic vesicular-trafficking modulation (Hap1) — all converging on **mTORC1** as a central metabolic integrator. This notebook is the transcriptional anchor for tri-modal follow-up (Augur, scFEA, pseudobulk).

## Background

WildR and SPF mice differ in lifetime microbiome exposure. WildR animals are more socially affiliative; the molecular question is whether the microbiome sculpts limbic gene expression along **region-specific** and **cell-type-specific** axes rather than uniformly.

**Data and statistics.** DEGs come from snRNA-seq MAST testing across Allen MapMyCells supertypes (class, subclass, and supertype levels screened; this notebook focuses on supertype). Each gene in the summary table reports minimum adjusted p-value across supertypes, effect direction (WildR-UP vs SPF-UP), tissue of the strongest hit, and count of significant supertypes (`n_signif`). For visualization we take the 75 most significant unique genes (padj \< 0.05, \|log2 FC\| \> 0.25), map them onto recurrently significant supertypes, and hierarchically cluster rows and columns on log2 fold-change. Source narrative: [interpretations/WildR_vs_SPF_DEG_Report.docx]{.path}.

## Results

[**Figure 1.**]{.fig-num} Clustered dot-plot heatmap of the top 75 DEGs across supertypes with recurrent significance. Rows (genes) and columns (supertypes) are hierarchically clustered on log2 fold-change; dot size encodes −log₁₀(padj) and fill encodes log2 FC (WildR-up vs SPF-up, scico *cork* palette). Columns are faceted by tissue (AMY, HYP).
:::

::: {.takeaways}
**Key takeaways**

- **Structural dissociation in the heatmap:** Cmss1 and Lars2 produce dense SPF-UP rows across nearly every hypothalamic supertype; amygdalar hits are comparatively supertype-restricted — implying different mechanisms of microbiome influence in AMY vs HYP.
- **Five convergent storylines:** (1) pan-hypothalamic translational hyperactivation in SPF (Cmss1/Lars2 → mitochondrial translation, mTORC1/AMPK); (2) amygdalar synaptic remodeling (contactins, protocadherins, actin regulators); (3) opposing calcium-signaling programs (Calm1/Ryr3 WildR-UP vs Trpm3/Camk1d SPF-UP); (4) epigenetic/splicing reprogramming (Zbtb16, Hdac9, Srrm2); (5) hypothalamic vesicular trafficking (Hap1 SPF-UP across 17 supertypes).
- **mTORC1 is the integrator:** Cmss1/Lars2 (translational output), Prex2 (PI3K/Akt input), Hap1 (trafficking), and Mid1 (PP2A–mTOR axis) converge on metabolic translational control in both regions.
- **Breadth vs depth by tissue:** HYP — 55% of supertypes with ≥1 DEG but only 4% with ≥10; AMY — 31% with ≥1 but 16% with ≥10 — consistent with pan-hypothalamic metabolic shifts vs focal amygdalar circuit remodeling.
- **Behavioral circuits:** AMY modules map to SDMN, hippocampal output, and claustrum salience ("memory, meaning, mood"); HYP modules map to Papez context, MPN affiliation, SUM novelty, and ZI/AHN defensive brakes ("defense to connection").
:::

### Supertype hit burden by tissue

At supertype resolution (padj \< 0.05, \|coef\| \> 0.25), **164** supertypes were tested in AMY and **225** in HYP. AMY shows fewer supertypes with any DEG but a larger share with deep alteration; HYP shows broader low-level involvement.

| Tissue | Tested | ≥1 DEG | ≥10 DEGs |
|--------|-------:|-------:|---------:|
| AMY | 164 | 51 (31%) | 26 (16%) |
| HYP | 225 | 124 (55%) | 9 (4%) |

### Reading the heatmap: pan-hypothalamic vs supertype-specific amygdalar effects

The dot plot's most important structural feature is the contrast between **dense hypothalamic rows** (one gene, many supertypes) and **sparse amygdalar rows** (one gene, discrete populations). Cmss1 (padj = 5.43×10⁻⁷³, **123** significant supertypes) and Lars2 (padj = 1.15×10⁻²⁵, **53** supertypes) dominate — both SPF-UP, both mitochondrial translational machinery. This is not cell-type-specific noise; it is a fundamental hypothalamic metabolic shift gated by microbiome status. Amygdalar top hits, by contrast, tend to affect named circuit elements (BLA, CeA, MEA, LA) one supertype at a time.

### 1. Pan-hypothalamic translational hyperactivation (Cmss1–Lars2)

**Cmss1** encodes a mitochondrial tRNA 2-thiouridylase (wobble-position modification); **Lars2** encodes mitochondrial leucyl-tRNA synthetase. Together they define a mitochondrial translational hyperactivation program in SPF hypothalamic neurons.

**Mechanistic model.** Microbiome-derived SCFAs (especially butyrate) act as HDAC inhibitors and AMPK activators, tonically restraining hypothalamic mTORC1 in WildR mice. In SPF mice lacking this metabolite brake, mTORC1 is derepressed → compensatory upregulation of mitochondrial translational machinery across **123** supertypes. This argues for **systemic** metabolite action on hypothalamic tissue, not narrow receptor-specific mechanisms.

**Functional stakes.** Hypothalamic neurons integrate leptin, ghrelin, insulin, and glucose to coordinate feeding, autonomic output, and neuroendocrine function. Enhanced mitochondrial translation in SPF may alter neuropeptide synthesis in ARH (AgRP/POMC), stress peptides in PVH (CRH), or metabolic sensing in VMH *Nr5a1*⁺ neurons — populations previously implicated as microbiome targets.

### 2. Amygdalar synaptic architecture and adhesion molecules

A contactin/protocadherin/actin cluster dominates the amygdalar landscape. The amygdala gates threat detection, fear learning, and social valence: LA (fear conditioning), BLA (contextual integration), CeA (behavioral fear output), MEA (pheromonal/social processing). Differential adhesion-molecule expression implies the microbiome influences which synapses form, stabilize, or are pruned.

| Gene | Direction | Tissue | Role | n_sig |
|------|-----------|--------|------|------:|
| *Cttnbp2* | WildR-UP | AMY | Spine morphogenesis; ASD-associated | 10 |
| *Cntn6* | WildR-UP | HYP | Axon guidance; GABAergic synapse specificity | 3 |
| *Pcdh7* | WildR-UP | AMY | Dendritic self-avoidance | 1 |
| *Cdh12* | WildR-UP | AMY | Homophilic adhesion; synaptic specificity | 1 |
| *Ncam1* | SPF-UP | AMY | Synaptic plasticity; LTP | 2 |
| *Negr1* | SPF-UP | AMY | Growth regulator; depression/obesity GWAS | 2 |
| *Slit2* | SPF-UP | AMY | Axon repulsion (Robo) | 2 |

WildR mice show active dendritic remodeling (*Cttnbp2* across 10 supertypes, *Eps8l1* across 16 — actin dynamics). SPF mice engage alternative programs (*Ncam1*, *Cntn4*). *Cttnbp2* mutations are linked to ASD in humans, directly connecting microbiome-dependent spine remodeling to social-behavior circuits.

### 3. Calcium signaling and excitability (amygdala)

| Component | Direction | Implication |
|-----------|-----------|-------------|
| *Calm1* | WildR-UP (n=3) | Enhanced Ca²⁺-dependent plasticity (CaMKII, calcineurin) |
| *Ryr3* | WildR-UP | Amplified ER CICR — relevant for thalamo-amygdalar LTP |
| *Trpm3* | SPF-UP | Neurosteroid-gated Ca²⁺ influx; compensatory entry |
| *Camk1d*, *Itpkb* | SPF-UP | Compensatory kinase/IP3 signaling |

**Net picture:** WildR amygdalar neurons are primed for robust ER-mediated calcium signaling; SPF neurons shift toward non-synaptic entry and compensatory kinase activity — with direct implications for fear learning, extinction, and anxiety.

### 4. Hypothalamic homeostasis: Hap1 and ion channels

**Hap1** (SPF-UP, padj = 4.42×10⁻¹⁴, **17** supertypes) mediates GABA_A receptor, TrkB, and feeding-receptor trafficking. Hap1 KO mice are postnatal lethal with severe hypothalamic feeding deficits. Combined with Cmss1/Lars2 upregulation, SPF hypothalamic neurons appear to simultaneously **make more protein and traffic more aggressively** — consistent with metabolic dysregulation in the absence of microbial satiety signals.

WildR hypothalamic neurons show opposing ion-channel tuning: **Kcnb2/Kv2.2** and **Kcnn2/SK2** (WildR-UP) support high-fidelity, patterned firing (relevant for pulsatile PVH CRH/TRH release). SPF neurons may fire more broadly and less precisely — affecting neuroendocrine pulsatility and circadian output.

### 5. Epigenetic and transcriptional reprogramming (amygdala)

- **Zbtb16/PLZF** (WildR-UP, padj = 7.67×10⁻²⁰, n=7): recruits HDAC/NCoR complexes; retinoic-acid responsive — microbial vitamin A metabolism may influence amygdalar transcription.
- **Hdac9** (SPF-UP): class IIa HDAC shuttling with CaMKII — links aberrant calcium-to-chromatin signaling in SPF.
- **Bhlhe40/Dec1** (WildR-UP, n=4): circadian repressor — microbiome may entrain amygdalar clock genes.
- **Srrm2** (WildR-UP, n=11): splicing coactivator — broad RNA-processing shift across amygdalar supertypes.

**Ras/MAPK tug-of-war (amygdala):** *Rasgef1a* (SPF-UP, n=5) loads Ras-GTP → higher basal ERK signaling in SPF; *Rasa1* (WildR-UP, n=4) stimulates GTP hydrolysis → Ras brake in WildR. In hypothalamus, *Prex2* (SPF-UP) suppresses PTEN and amplifies PI3K/Akt → mTORC1 (see below).

### 6. High-priority enigmatic genes

- **ENSMUSG00000095041** (WildR-UP, padj = 1.33×10⁻²⁷, **37** supertypes): second-most significant hit genome-wide; unannotated; widest amygdalar spread. Priority for ncRNA annotation, conservation, and chromatin context.
- **Mid1** (WildR-UP; AMY n=21, HYP n=15): E3 ligase degrading PP2A → derepresses mTOR; mechanistic bridge to Cmss1/Lars2 story.
- **Prex2** (SPF-UP, HYP, padj = 4.92×10⁻²⁰): Rac-GEF, PTEN suppressor → PI3K/Akt → mTORC1 activation in SPF hypothalamus.

### 7. Integrated model: microbiome as limbic systems modulator

::: {.callout-note}
**Hypothalamic metabolic program (SPF vs WildR).** WildR: lower basal mitochondrial translation, Mid1-tuned PP2A/mTOR, precise neuroendocrine firing (Kv2.2, SK2), moderate Hap1 trafficking. SPF: pan-hypothalamic translational surge, aggressive Hap1-driven trafficking, Prex2-disinhibited PI3K/Akt — consistent with germ-free/SPF metabolic phenotypes (body composition, insulin sensitivity, feeding).
:::

::: {.callout-note}
**Amygdalar connectivity program.** WildR: active spine remodeling (Cttnbp2, Eps8l1), robust ER calcium (Calm1, Ryr3), PLZF repression (Zbtb16), altered splicing (Srrm2). SPF: alternative adhesion (Ncam1, Cntn4), Trpm3 calcium entry, Hdac9 chromatin shifts — a different synaptic landscape underlying altered fear, anxiety, and social interaction.
:::

**mTORC1 convergence** is the mechanistic anchor: hypothalamus (Cmss1/Lars2 output, Prex2 input, Hap1 trafficking) and amygdala (Mid1–PP2A axis) independently tune the master integrator of metabolic state and translational capacity.

:::: {.section-rule}
::::

### Circuit-level interpretation: socially annotated supertypes

The gene-level modules above land on specific Allen supertypes. Tissue-specific circuit narratives ([interpretations/DEG_snRNASeq_AMY.md]{.path}, [interpretations/DEG_snRNASeq_HY.md]{.path}) connect molecular shifts to behavior.

#### Amygdala — "Memory, meaning, and mood"

Unlike HYP (drive and state), AMY is about **recognition and interpretation** — processing *who* and *how it feels*.

1. **Social memory output (CA1–ProS, CA3):** Prosubiculum is the hippocampal output gate to BLA/MEA/BST; CA3 drives one-shot social learning. Enrichment here → faster conspecific categorization, dampened neophobia.
2. **Pheromone-to-action bridge (MEA–BST, COA):** Core SDMN hub; MEA reads vomeronasal input, BST executes aggression/mating/parenting. WildR shift → pheromones interpreted as affiliative rather than threatening; *Sox6*/*Lhx6* GABAergic brakes on aggression.
3. **Olfactory-limbic interface (ENT, COA, RHP):** COA mediates innate odor-driven behavior; WildR may assign reward valence to conspecific scent vs SPF "irritation" from neuroimmune activation.
4. **Salience hub (claustrum *Car3*):** Social partner becomes a high-salience, worth-exploring stimulus.
5. **Synthesis:** Better recognition → re-interpreted scent → higher engagement. Microbiome remodels SDMN toward **curiosity over defensiveness**.

#### Hypothalamus — "Defense to connection"

Focused alteration in spatial/context memory, sexual/parental behavior, and inhibitory motor control.

1. **Mammillary body / Papez (MM, *Foxb1*⁺):** Contextual social memory — mapping "who" to "where"; less territorial anxiety.
2. **Preoptic hub (MPN, AVPV):** Affiliation switch; MPN balances mating vs fighting — WildR tipped toward affiliative investigatory behavior.
3. **Zona incerta (*Pax6*⁺ GABA):** Suppresses innate fear; allows approach without flight.
4. **Supramammillary (SUM):** SUM–CA2 social novelty pathway — "smoking gun" for enhanced social curiosity.
5. **Defense vs drive (AHN, LHA–MEA):** AHN brake on defensive rage; LHA–MEA wires pheromone smell to reward not threat.
6. **Synthesis:** Threat suppressed (ZI/AHN) → context/novelty clear (MM/SUM) → affiliative drive engaged (MPN/LHA). **High-trust / low-fear** hypothalamic state.

The gut microbiome emerges from this analysis as an active sculptor of limbic circuit gene expression — not via narrow receptor mechanisms but through **systemic modulation** of neuronal transcriptional programs (123 hypothalamic supertypes for Cmss1 alone). mTORC1 provides the mechanistic anchor integrating diverse gene-level findings. ENSMUSG00000095041 — entirely unannotated, pan-amygdalar — highlights discovery potential remaining in this dataset. Together, these molecular programs establish a foundation for WildR vs SPF behavioral phenotypes and position cell-type-resolved transcriptomics as a primary tool for dissecting microbiome–brain communication.

## Next Steps

### Completed in this notebook

- Cell-type-resolved ranking of top 75 DEGs with supertype burden quantification and clustered heatmap visualization.
- Molecular interpretation framework (translational, synaptic, calcium, epigenetic, mTORC1 convergence) tied to socially annotated circuits.

### Proposed follow-up experiments (from DEG report)

1. **SCFA rescue:** Administer butyrate to SPF mice; test whether Cmss1/Lars2 normalize across hypothalamic supertypes (metabolite sufficiency for translational set-point).
2. **mTORC1 IHC:** Phospho-S6K1 and phospho-4E-BP1 in WildR vs SPF hypothalamus; co-stain *Nr5a1* (VMH), AgRP/POMC (ARH), CRH (PVH).
3. **ENSMUSG00000095041 characterization:** ncRNA databases, ATAC-seq, neighbor-gene correlation (37-supertype breadth = top priority).
4. **Cttnbp2 spine analysis:** Golgi or diolistic labeling in BLA/CeA to quantify spine density/morphology in WildR vs SPF.
5. **Electrophysiology:** VMH *Nr5a1*⁺ and ARH AgRP⁺ neurons — firing frequency, spike adaptation (Kv2.2), mAHP (SK2), spontaneous synaptic currents.
6. **Hap1 conditional KO:** *Hap1* flox × hypothalamic Cre (*Nr5a1*-Cre, AgRP-Cre) in WildR and SPF backgrounds.
7. **Circadian profiling:** Time-resolved RNA-seq at multiple Zeitgeber times (motivated by *Bhlhe40* DE).

### Computational tri-modal integration

- Cut heatmap row clusters → g:Profiler per module × tissue ([0X_PathwayAnalysis.qmd]{.path}).
- Overlay Augur AUROC on heatmap columns ([0X_Augur_SN.qmd]{.path}); pseudobulk EdgeR/DESeq2 validation ([0X_PseudoBulk_SN.qmd]{.path}).
- scFEA flux on DEG- and Augur-prioritized strata ([0X_FluxAnalysis.qmd]{.path}).
- SeqFISH spatial validation and CellChat ligand–receptor analysis ([01_QC_prep_SeqFISH.qmd]{.path}, [12_CellChat.qmd]{.path}).

```{r}
save_table_artifacts <- function(df, csv_path, html_path = NULL, preview_n = 20) {
  readr::write_csv(df, csv_path)
  if (!is.null(html_path)) {
    preview <- utils::head(df, preview_n)
    html_out <- paste0(
      "<!DOCTYPE html><html><head><meta charset=\"utf-8\">",
      "<style>table{border-collapse:collapse;font-size:12px}",
      "td,th{border:1px solid #ddd;padding:4px 8px}</style>",
      "</head><body>",
      knitr::kable(preview, format = "html", escape = FALSE),
      "</body></html>"
    )
    writeLines(html_out, html_path, useBytes = TRUE)
  }
  invisible(df)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: cell-load-seurat
#| eval: !expr run_analysis

seurat_obj <- readRDS(
  glue("{data_path}/seurat/snRNASeq/",
       "seurat_obj_onlyparsefilters_celltyped_2025-12-27.rds")
)
seurat_obj <- seurat_obj %>% subset(subset = keep_cell)

allen_annot_df <- seurat_obj@meta.data %>%
  select(class_name, class_label, subclass_name,
         subclass_label, supertype_name, supertype_label) %>%
  distinct()

allen_annot_long <- allen_annot_df %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = c("cell_type_level", ".value"),
    names_pattern = "(class|subclass|supertype)_(name|label)"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::rename(cell_type_name = name, cell_type_label = label) %>%
  distinct()
```

```{r}
#| label: cell-load-mast
#| eval: !expr run_analysis

format_mastdf <- function(mast_df, name_col, level_col) {
  mast_df %>%
    dplyr::rename(cell_type_name = {{name_col}}) %>%
    janitor::clean_names() %>%
    mutate(cell_type_level = {{level_col}})
}

class_mast_df <- readRDS(
  glue("{data_path}/mast/snRNASeq/class_mast_signif_hits_2026-01-04.rds")
) %>%
  format_mastdf(name_col = "class_name", level_col = "class")

subclass_mast_df <- readRDS(
  glue("{data_path}/mast/snRNASeq/subclass_mast_signif_hits_2026-01-04.rds")
) %>%
  format_mastdf(name_col = "subclass_name", level_col = "subclass")

supertype_mast_df <- readRDS(
  glue("{data_path}/mast/snRNASeq/supertype_mast_signif_hits_2026-01-04.rds")
) %>%
  format_mastdf(name_col = "supertype_name", level_col = "supertype")

mast_df <- bind_rows(class_mast_df, subclass_mast_df, supertype_mast_df) %>%
  filter(p_adjust < 0.05) %>%
  mutate(
    gene = gsub("-GRCm39", "", primerid),
    direction = if_else(coef > 0, "WildR-UP", "SPF-UP")
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: cell-stats-celltypes
#| eval: !expr run_analysis

celltype_droplist <- readRDS(
  glue("{data_path}/seurat/snRNASeq/celltype_droplist_2025-12-30.rds")
)

metadata_df <- seurat_obj@meta.data

batchparams_df <- bind_rows(
  metadata_df %>%
    dplyr::select(celltype = class_label, tissue) %>%
    distinct() %>%
    mutate(cell_type_column = "class_label"),
  metadata_df %>%
    dplyr::select(celltype = subclass_label, tissue) %>%
    distinct() %>%
    mutate(cell_type_column = "subclass_label"),
  metadata_df %>%
    dplyr::select(celltype = supertype_label, tissue) %>%
    distinct() %>%
    mutate(cell_type_column = "supertype_label")
) %>%
  left_join(celltype_droplist) %>%
  filter(is.na(dropme)) %>%
  dplyr::select(cell_type_column, celltype, tissue)

n_tested_AMY_supt <- batchparams_df %>%
  filter(tissue == "AMY", cell_type_column == "supertype_label") %>%
  distinct(celltype) %>%
  nrow()

n_tested_HYP_supt <- batchparams_df %>%
  filter(tissue == "HYP", cell_type_column == "supertype_label") %>%
  distinct(celltype) %>%
  nrow()

deg_burden <- mast_df %>%
  filter(p_adjust < 0.05, abs(coef) > 0.25, cell_type_level == "supertype") %>%
  group_by(tissue, cell_type_name) %>%
  tally(name = "n_deg") %>%
  group_by(tissue) %>%
  summarise(
    tested = dplyr::if_else(tissue == "AMY", n_tested_AMY_supt, n_tested_HYP_supt),
    n_ge1 = sum(n_deg >= 1),
    n_ge10 = sum(n_deg >= 10),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    pct_ge1 = round(100 * n_ge1 / tested, 1),
    pct_ge10 = round(100 * n_ge10 / tested, 1)
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: cell-prep-heatmap
#| eval: !expr run_analysis

top_75_genes <- mast_df %>%
  filter(cell_type_level == "supertype") %>%
  filter(p_adjust < 0.05, abs(coef) > 0.25) %>%
  arrange(p_adjust) %>%
  pull(gene) %>%
  unique() %>%
  head(75)

significant_celltypes <- mast_df %>%
  filter(cell_type_level == "supertype") %>%
  filter(gene %in% top_75_genes) %>%
  group_by(cell_type_name) %>%
  tally() %>%
  filter(n > 1) %>%
  pull(cell_type_name) %>%
  unique()

top_mast_df <- mast_df %>%
  filter(cell_type_level == "supertype") %>%
  arrange(p_adjust) %>%
  head(200) %>%
  mutate(neglog10_p = -log10(p_adjust))

plot_df <- mast_df %>%
  filter(primerid %in% paste0(top_75_genes, "-GRCm39")) %>%
  filter(cell_type_name %in% significant_celltypes) %>%
  mutate(
    gene = gsub("-GRCm39", "", primerid),
    neglog10_p = -log10(p_adjust)
  )

clust_mat <- plot_df %>%
  dplyr::select(gene, celltype_tissue, coef) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = celltype_tissue,
    values_from = coef,
    values_fill = 0
  ) %>%
  tibble::column_to_rownames("gene") %>%
  as.matrix()

row_order <- hclust(dist(clust_mat), method = "ward.D2")$order
col_order <- hclust(dist(t(clust_mat)), method = "ward.D2")$order

gene_levels <- rownames(clust_mat)[row_order]
celltype_levels <- colnames(clust_mat)[col_order]

plot_df <- plot_df %>%
  mutate(
    gene = factor(gene, levels = gene_levels),
    celltype_tissue = factor(celltype_tissue, levels = celltype_levels)
  )

ct_labels <- plot_df %>%
  distinct(celltype_tissue, cell_type_name) %>%
  deframe()
```

```{r}
#| label: cell-fig-heatmap
#| eval: !expr run_analysis
#| fig-show: hide

coef_lim <- max(abs(top_mast_df$coef), na.rm = TRUE)

p_heatmap <- plot_df %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = celltype_tissue, y = gene, size = neglog10_p)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.9, shape = 21, aes(fill = coef)) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = ct_labels) +
  scale_fill_scico(
    palette = "cork",
    midpoint = 0,
    limits = c(-coef_lim, coef_lim)
  ) +
  scale_size_continuous(
    range = c(2, 8),
    name = expression(-log[10](p[adj]))
  ) +
  facet_grid(~ tissue, scales = "free", space = "free") +
  labs(
    x = "Supertype",
    y = "Gene",
    fill = "log2 FC",
    title = glue(
      "Top 75 DEG hits: {length(top_75_genes)} genes x {length(significant_celltypes)} supertypes"
    )
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 8),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7, face = "italic"),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(linewidth = 0.2, color = "grey90"),
    legend.position = "right",
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold")
  )
```

```{r}
cell_type_level <- "supertype"

high_hit_combos <- supertype_mast %>%
  group_by(cell_type_name, tissue) %>%
  tally() %>%
  filter(n >= min_hits_per_celltype_tissue) %>%
  select(cell_type_name, tissue)

top_by_p <- supertype_mast %>%
  arrange(p_adjust) %>%
  head(top_n) %>%
  select(gene, cell_type_name, tissue, direction)

high_hit_genes <- supertype_mast %>%
  semi_join(high_hit_combos, by = c("cell_type_name", "tissue")) %>%
  select(gene, cell_type_name, tissue, direction)

violin_hits <- bind_rows(top_by_p, high_hit_genes) %>%
  distinct(gene, cell_type_name, tissue, direction) %>%
  mutate(
    cell_type_name_clean = gsub("/", "-", cell_type_name) %>% gsub(" ", "_", .)
  )

violin_hits_grouped <- violin_hits %>%
  filter(gene %nin% c("Pakap-2")) %>%
  group_by(cell_type_name, cell_type_name_clean, tissue) %>%
  summarise(genes = list(tibble(gene, direction)), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r}
#| label: cell-violin-plots
#| eval: false

# Heavy export loop — set eval: true to regenerate violin plots.
# Outputs: figures/DEG/snRNASeq/top_hits/supertype/{tissue}/{celltype}/{gene}_{direction}_{tissue}_{celltype}.png

violin_out_base <- glue("{fig_path}/DEG/snRNASeq/top_hits/{cell_type_level}")
registerDoParallel(7)

for (g in seq_len(nrow(violin_hits_grouped))) {
  celltype_index <- violin_hits_grouped$cell_type_name[g]
  celltype <- violin_hits_grouped$cell_type_name_clean[g]
  tissue <- violin_hits_grouped$tissue[g]
  gene_dir <- violin_hits_grouped$genes[[g]]
  genes <- gene_dir$gene

  multi_df <- get_gene_expression_df_multi(
    seurat_obj,
    celltype_column = celltype_column,
    celltype_value = celltype_index,
    genes = genes,
    tissue = tissue,
    return_format = "log2cpm"
  )

  if (nrow(multi_df) == 0) {
    warning(glue("No cells for {celltype} / {tissue}; skipping {length(genes)} genes"))
    next
  }

  multi_df <- multi_df %>%
    mutate(sample = factor(sample, levels = unique(sample[order(microbiome, sample)])))

  .multi_df <- multi_df
  .gene_dir <- gene_dir
  .tissue <- tissue
  .celltype <- celltype
  .out_base <- violin_out_base

  foreach(
    j = seq_len(nrow(.gene_dir)),
    .packages = c("ggplot2", "glue", "dplyr"),
    .export = c(
      ".multi_df", ".gene_dir", ".tissue", ".celltype", ".out_base",
      "plot_gene_expression"
    )
  ) %dopar% {
    genename <- .gene_dir$gene[j]
    direction <- .gene_dir$direction[j]
    out_dir <- glue("{.out_base}/{.tissue}/{.celltype}")
    fname <- glue("{genename}_{direction}_{.tissue}_{.celltype}.png")
    full_fig_path <- file.path(out_dir, fname)

    if (file.exists(full_fig_path)) return(NULL)
    dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

    p_combined <- plot_gene_expression(
      .multi_df,
      gene = genename,
      tissue = .tissue,
      celltype_value = .celltype
    )
    ggsave(full_fig_path, p_combined, width = 8, height = 5)
    NULL
  }
}
```


```{r}
#| label: cell-get-gene-expression
#| eval: false

# Get gene expression vectors for Lars 2 and CMS1 from each cell type where they are significant in the hypothalamus.
mast_df %>% glimpse()
cmss1_lars_sig_hyp_supert <- mast_df %>% 
  filter(gene %in% c("Cmss1")) %>% 
  filter(tissue == "HYP") %>%
  filter(cell_type_level == "supertype") %>%
  slice_min(p_adjust, n = 20) %>%
  pull(cell_type_name) %>%
  unique()
  

cmss1_lars2_expression_df <- tibble()
for (celltype in cmss1_lars_sig_hyp_supert) {
  print(glue("Getting expression for {celltype}"))
  gene_df <- get_gene_expression_df_multi(
    seurat_obj,
    celltype_column = "supertype_name",
    celltype_value = celltype,
    gene = c("Lars2", "Cmss1"),
    tissue = "HYP",
    return_format = "log2cpm")
  cmss1_lars2_expression_df <- bind_rows(cmss1_lars2_expression_df, gene_df)
}

cmss1_lars2_expression_df %>% glimpse()

p_cmss1_lars2_cor <- cmss1_lars2_expression_df %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = Cmss1_log2cpm, y = Lars2_log2cpm)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.1) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  ggpubr::stat_cor(method = "pearson") +
  ggpubr::stat_regline_equation(label.x.npc = 0.05, label.y.npc = 0.91) +
  facet_wrap(~ supertype_name) +
  theme_bw() +
  coord_fixed() +
  labs(x = "Cmss1 Expression", y = "Lars2 Expression") 

ggsave(
  glue("{fig_path}/DEG/snRNASeq/misc/cmss1_lars2_cor_{Sys.Date()}.png"),
  p_cmss1_lars2_cor,
  width = 12,
  height = 12,
  dpi = 300
)
```
